div.div: A visit is a small state machine: every offering hangs off one hub and is offered at most once, so every visit provably ends; the language model only supplies the words inside each state (3 illustrative offerings [I1])

CHAT
offering 1

A SMALL GIFT
offering 2 (self-serve)

A PHOTO
offering 3 (visitor's phone)

WAITING
(attract posture)

ARRIVAL
generic hello, never the last word: always followed by one specific thing

OFFER HUB
the robot raises ONE offering, or the visitor asks for one; all offerings are equals

CELEBRATE
a reaction, brief; only with something safe now, else skip silently

NO ANSWER
name one SPECIFIC thing (never an open 'what would you like?')

JUST TALKING
repeated decline or 'I'm fine': offering stops, the robot stays warm

CLOSING
goodbye; every offering mentioned at least once

RESET (close the visit)
confirmed stop of speech and motion, then delete ALL per-visit state

NEEDS STAFF
reset could not be confirmed: no new visit on top
Steps out of view and returns within a short window = the SAME visit: no fresh hello, no repeated offers.
each offering returns to the hub; offerings never connect to each other
GLOBAL: the visitor walks away -> CLOSING, from any state. A silence is not a departure; a departure is never answered as a silence.
GLOBAL: SAFETY PAUSE pre-empts every state and stays stopped until staff clear it; the hardware power cut is never a software call.
THE RULES THAT MUST ALWAYS HOLD (invariants)

1 The robot offers first: the visit never depends on the visitor knowing what to ask.
2 Silence never strands the visit: name one specific thing.
3 One thing at a time: one offering per turn, never a list (unless asked 'what can you do?').
4 A no is a no: a declined offering is not raised again; a repeated decline stops all offering.
5 Nothing stays a secret: every offering is MENTIONED once before goodbye (unless the visitor left, declined or asked to stop).
6 Offering always runs out: each offering is OFFERED at most once, so the visit terminates.
7 Celebration is a reaction, never a request, and never reopens what 4 or 6 closed.
8 The robot never claims to remember anyone: after the reset a returning person is a stranger.

MENTION vs OFFER: two flags, never one.
A mention says a thing exists and expects no answer; an offer names it and waits for yes or no. Rule 5 is discharged by a mention; rule 6 caps offers. Merge the flags and one of the two rules breaks.

THE HUB TRACKS, per visit (all deleted by the reset): offerings available now, mentioned, offered, declined; consecutive unanswered offers; whether offering is still permitted; whether a celebration is possible; the offering completed last (never offered next). A celebration changes none of these.

Legend: blue = visit states | green = offerings (solid arrow = raised or asked, dashed = back to the hub) | amber = no-answer and celebration paths | red = safety and staff states. Transition hygiene: stop BEFORE start; the stop is confirmed, not assumed.

Sources. Every number is loaded from ../constants.json by the key shown. [Pn] = public (a paper, standard or physics value, or my arithmetic on one); [In] = illustrative (a round design value of the right order; never a measurement of a real robot or visitor); [calc] = my arithmetic on tagged values.
Mechanism: notes/A1-the-experience-as-a-state-machine.md (overview states, arrival, offer hub, following the lead, celebrating and closing, the eight invariants, state the hub must track, transition hygiene); B1 (safety supervisor above the state machine). Termination argument: a finite offering set with at most one offer each ends every visit (A1, 'How it is designed and tested').
[I1] offerings_illustrative = 3 offerings (chat, a small gift, a photo). illustrative offering set
